description: Retrieve the full text of one LOC page — a historical newspaper page, or a book or manuscript page — or, with match, only the passages around your search terms, with its publication metadata: for newspapers the title, issue date, place of publication, indexed states, and edition; for every page its sequence, the page count, and the item_title and item_id of the issue, book, or manuscript it belongs to — pass item_id to libofcongress_get_item to list every page of the item. Pass the url field from a libofcongress_search_newspapers result, or a pages[].page_url from libofcongress_get_item (has_text true), or a Chronicling America page link (…/ed-N/seq-M/) — do not construct this URL manually. A dense newspaper page runs to 50,000 characters: to find the article a search hit on, pass the search query as match and read the passages around it rather than the whole page. The text is OCR, or for some manuscripts a volunteer transcription; OCR quality varies by digitization batch and era, and 19th-century and degraded materials may contain fragmented text, garbled words, and line-break artifacts that are surfaced as-is. When a page exists but has no digitized text, ocr_available is false and ocr_text is empty — this is a data property, not an error.

match.description: Return the passages around these terms instead of the whole page — pass the query you gave libofcongress_search_newspapers (e.g., titanic, or "the titanic" iceberg); the q= in a search result url is not read as match. Words separated by spaces are separate terms, any of which matches; a double-quoted span is one phrase. Each matches case-insensitively as literal text, with line breaks read as spaces; OCR misreads are not repaired. When set, ocr_text is empty, matches holds up to 10 passages of about 300 characters either side of each occurrence — when they need more, occurrences of the rarest terms come first, so a common word only fills the slots left — and match_count counts every occurrence. Omit match for the whole page. Up to 200 characters; blank is ignored.

page_url.description: A LOC page URL: the url field from a libofcongress_search_newspapers result (e.g., "https://www.loc.gov/resource/sn83045462/1905-03-15/ed-1/?sp=1"), or a pages[].page_url from libofcongress_get_item for a newspaper, book, or manuscript page (e.g., "https://www.loc.gov/resource/mss93930.mss93930-001/?sp=3"). Also accepted: the same /resource/ URL over http or without "www.", a newspaper page path ending /ed-N/seq-M/, and a Chronicling America page link (`chroniclingamerica.loc.gov/lccn/<lccn>/<date>/ed-N/seq-M/`); each is read as its https://www.loc.gov/resource/…/?sp=M page. Pass the value as returned — do not construct page URLs.

name: libofcongress_get_newspaper_page

edition.description: Edition number of the issue (e.g., "1"). Absent when LOC gives none.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `invalid_page_url`: page_url is not one LOC page: neither a loc.gov /resource/ URL nor a Chronicling America page link ending /ed-N/seq-M/. `page_not_found`: The URL does not resolve to a LOC page resource. `rate_limit_exceeded`: LOC API rate limit exceeded; requests are blocked for approximately 1 hour. `server_busy`: More Library of Congress requests are queued on this server than can start within this call's time budget. `request_timed_out`: The Library of Congress did not respond within the 50-second request budget. `upstream_unavailable`: The Library of Congress could not be reached, or answered with an error status, a bot challenge or other HTML page, or an unreadable response instead of its JSON. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

item_id.description: ID of the item this page belongs to: the newspaper issue (e.g., "sn83030214/1912-04-16/ed-1"), book, or manuscript volume (e.g., "mm77093930"). Pass it to libofcongress_get_item to list every page of the item, each with its page_url and has_text — for an article continued on a later page, or the next page of a book. Absent when LOC names no item.

item_title.description: Title of the item this page belongs to, on every page type: the book or manuscript title, or for a newspaper page the issue title with place and date (e.g., "New-York tribune (New York [N.Y.]), April 16, 1912"). Absent when LOC gives none.

match_count.description: Present only when match is set: occurrences of every match term on the page, including those beyond the passages returned. 0 when nothing matched or the page has no text.

matches.description: Present only when match is set: passages of the page text around the occurrences of the match terms, in page order — about 300 characters either side of each occurrence, overlapping passages merged up to 1,200 characters, never overlapping, at most 10, chosen around the rarest terms first when more would be needed. Empty when nothing matched or the page has no text.

newspaper_title.description: Title of the newspaper publication. Absent when LOC gives none.

notice.description: Set when ocr_available is true but the page's text came back empty, saying why: the text service did not answer this call (retry), its answer could not be read as text (retrying will not help), or the page's text is empty — a blank page, including one LOC sends as the placeholder [NO TEXT AVAILABLE FOR THIS PAGE]. Distinguishes these from a genuinely image-only page (where ocr_available is false), which carries no notice. With match set on a page that has text, set instead when nothing matched or when some occurrences fall outside the passages returned — those are read on the whole page, by calling again without match. Absent otherwise.

ocr_available.description: True when LOC lists OCR or transcribed text for this page, even if the text it returns is empty (see notice). False for image-only pages where no text has been produced.

ocr_text.description: Full plain text of this page: OCR, or for some manuscripts a volunteer transcription. Empty string when match is set (read matches instead), when ocr_available is false, or when the page is blank or its text could not be retrieved (see notice). May contain fragmented words, line-break artifacts, and misspellings inherent to historical OCR — do not attempt to repair.

page_url.description: The LOC resource URL for this page, in the https://www.loc.gov/resource/…?sp=N form the input was read as.

place_of_publication.description: Where the newspaper was published, as LOC catalogs it (e.g., "Charleston, S.C."). Absent when LOC gives none.

segment_count.description: Number of pages in the issue, volume, or folder. Absent when LOC gives none.

sequence.description: Page sequence number within the issue, volume, or folder.

states.description: Every US state LOC indexes this newspaper title under (e.g., ["georgia", "south carolina"]), in LOC order — possibly more than the state of publication. Absent when LOC lists no state.

title: Get Newspaper Page
